To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
user participation in systems analysis and design has a positive impact on perceived participation, process satisfaction, and ownership, and a negative impact on intention to use.

(1) operational user participation in analysis and design has significant positive influence on perceived participation, (2) perceived participation has a positive influence on process satisfaction, perceived ownership, and intention-to-use and (3) operational user participation and perceived participation in the analysis phase has significant positive impact on perceived participation and intention-to-use, but not on process satisfaction and perceived-ownership.

user participation and desire for participation in analysis and design activities have a significant positive impact on perceived participation, which in turn, has a significant positive impact, in both the analysis and design stages, on process satisfaction and perceived system ownership.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of user participation in the system development life-cycle.
the role that operational end users play in the analysis and design of information systems.
the impact of user participation in two different stages of the system design process on the perceived participation, intention, process satisfaction, and perceived ownership of users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
user participation in analysis and design stages of the life cycles is important for the success of the system.

operational end user participation is a critical factor for perceived system implementation success and that participation in the analysis stages may be more important than participation in the design stages.
operational user participation in the different stages of the system life cycle is a significant factor in the success of the system development process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
operational end users should be given the opportunity to be actively involved in both analysis and design activities.

operational end user participation has a positive influence on system implementation success, and that user participation in analysis activities may be more important than participation in design activities.
operational users' participation in the analysis and design stages of a systems development project has a positive impact on their intention to use and perceived ownership of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
user participation is an important factor in the success of a project.
the participation of end users in the design and development process can have a profound impact on the success of the project and on the users’ perception of the system.
user participation is a key factor for successful system development projects.
